findings.where: Hero, the small tracked capitals under the name: 'INFRASTRUCTURE ADVISOR' over 'LONGITUDINAL SECTION A-A • SCALE NTS' (worst on phone, where the line breaks after 'A-A •' and leaves 'SCALE NTS' alone on the next line)
findings.fault: The one line that says what Mark does uses the same size, weight, case and tracking as the drawing's made-up annotation. Nothing in the type tells the visitor which is his role and which is decoration. On phone the annotation wraps with its bullet stranded at the end of a line.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer scanning the first screen to see who Mark is. 'Infrastructure advisor' reads as one more drawing label beside 'section A-A' and 'scale NTS', so his role gets lost in the sheet's decoration.

findings.where: Article specimen: the post title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law' compared with the Type pair card and the hero name
findings.fault: The tile's own type rule says 'Headings in ExtraBold capitals, tracked wide like a drawing title'. The hero name and section labels follow it, but the article heading is mixed case with no tracking. The tile states one heading style and shows two, without saying which applies to which level.
findings.who_objects: The layout-round designer and Angélique, who build every new post from this tile. They can't tell whether a post title should be set in tracked capitals or not, so article pages will drift apart.

findings.where: Article specimen: the byline 'MMM Infra Blog No. 8 • 18 September 2024' compared with the attachment line 'Lecture • 2026-04-23 · PDF'
findings.fault: Two dates in the same article are set differently. One is in sans with the month written out. The other is in Overpass Mono in ISO form, and the mono also covers the words 'Lecture' and 'PDF', although the type pair keeps mono for measurements only. The one line also mixes two separators, a bullet and a middle dot.
findings.who_objects: A reader of the post sees two date styles a few lines apart. Angélique, adding posts and PDFs, has no single pattern to copy for dates or labels.

findings.where: Running text set in Light on the blue ground: the article body, the palette swatch notes ('the ground', 'type, the cut, heavy lines'), the texture caption, the type-pair captions and the motion-sketch notes
findings.fault: Long reading text and the small captions use the Light weight, reversed out of a mid-blue patterned grid. Thin light strokes on a dark textured ground read weaker than the same size would in Regular. At caption size the notes look faint, and they sink into the grid lines behind them.
findings.who_objects: Readers of Mark's articles (the brief sets these pages to Read mode), many of them reading long posts on office laptops. Thin reversed text over a grid tires the eye over several paragraphs.

findings.where: Style-tile section labels ('PALETTE', 'TEXTURE', 'TYPE PAIR') compared with the swatch names beneath them ('DIAZO BLUE', 'LINEWORK', 'SODIUM AMBER')
findings.fault: Section labels and the item names inside each section share the same size, weight, case and tracking. The section label sits only one rule above its items, so two levels of the hierarchy read as one.
findings.who_objects: The layout-round designer, who takes the heading ranks from this tile. Few others would notice.

findings.where: Motion sketch: the easing paragraph and the timeline table (worst on phone)
findings.fault: The inline mono 'cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1)' looks larger than the sans around it. On phone it breaks in the middle of the value. In the table, the timings are in mono but the easing column's 'plot' is in bold sans, and the element names are heavier than the notes below them. Values that belong together are set three ways.
findings.who_objects: The animation-round designer reading the sketch, for whom the value and its row should read as a unit. Polish only.
